speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your post-operative review. I understand you had a tympanoplasty and are experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings; can you describe the exact location of the pain and how long it has been occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Incus dislocation (also known as disarticulation of the incudomalleolar joint).

The combination of shooting ear pain triggered by chewing and persistent discomfort with earrings, occurring 12 weeks after a right tympanoplasty, strongly suggests that the reconstructed ossicular chain has become disarticulated, causing mechanical irritation and conductive hearing symptoms despite previous improvement.
